pr.title: Write parts in bars and beats, land MIDI takes in ticks, and give the track its instrument (sequencer.md chunks 1–2)
pr.head: 14d0b3f54eb279cc3f846e1792274fd7bab2624a

summary: Field builds songs by rendering tracks and placing their audio on a timeline. This layer adds parts: editable files of notes that a track places in bars and beats, then renders through its instrument.

MIDI recordings now use the same notes format in ticks, so a tempo edit changes their playback timing. Their started_at_ticks counts from the record entry, so moving the entry moves its take. Older recordings marked with sample_rate: retain their original sample-based timing.
This is the notes and parts layer of the sequencer project. Live voices, scheduled MIDI output, and the sequencing command follow in separate layers.

cards.title: The files and their jobs
cards.html:
• Part: a notes file under a song’s notes/ directory.
  • Tick: musical time, with 960 ticks per quarter note.
  • Voice render: audio generated by playing resolved notes through an instrument.
  • Take: a recorded performance pinned by its content hash.

cards.title: Review evidence
cards.html:
Two models have reviewed this head. The newest review requests changes, so the pull request is a draft.

  • Still fixed: the earlier loop-timing finding. Each repetition resolves its notes at its own position.
  • Open findings: four, each flagged on its line below. A steady song renders one part many times at most tempos, notes played before a track starts all sound on its first tick, a documented step fails field check, and two edited lines break the surrounding line wrapping.
  • Checked in the newest review: type checking, project validation, and whitespace checks pass. The six test files nearest the change pass 140 of 140 against an existing field-audiod binary and real sclang.
  • Not run in the newest review: the other daemon tests, including live MIDI capture.

groups.title: Notes share one editable format
intro: A part contains notes, controller changes, and pitch bends. Its positions can use ticks or arrays of bars and beats, and its pitches can use MIDI numbers or scientific names such as C4. Recordings use scalar ticks; sample_rate: preserves the older recording format.

files.note: Defines note names, time spellings, defaults, and the one-row-per-event format.
Adds a track instrument and the notes entry kind.
Rejects instruments nested under record and adds the entry-relative started_at_ticks field for MIDI takes.
Allows flow maps and an unlimited line width for notes rows.

groups.title: A placement determines its note times
intro: A notes file can be placed at different points in a song. The resolver walks the placing track’s tempo and meter maps, then returns sample positions relative to that placement. Thus equal resolutions share a render, while a placement across a tempo change has different event timing.

files.note: Resolves part positions, lengths, and recorded-take anchors through the track clock.

checks.text: Resolver tests passed for meter changes, tempo changes, relative positions, note lengths, legacy sample-timed takes, and musical take anchors.

Open review finding: a steady song renders one part many times at most tempos. This line rounds a note's tick and the placement's tick to samples separately and then subtracts them, so a note's offset moves by a sample with where the part is placed whenever a bar is not a whole number of samples. At 133 bpm and 48 kHz, one part at bars 1 and 17 gets two action keys, the cache keys that decide whether a render is reused. A one-bar, 16-note loop of 32 repetitions makes 26 renders, each its own sclang run, where the plan and docs/project-model.md promise one. The fix is to round once, on the difference from the placement's start, and to add a test at 133 bpm, because the current tests use 120 bpm, where a tick is exactly 25 samples.

files.note: Exposes the meter in force at a tick.

groups.title: Parts become audio in the build graph
intro: The loader reads every part and the chosen MIDI take’s notes. Each placement resolves its notes through the track clock, including every occurrence of a loop. Occurrences with equal events share a voice render; a distinct resolution gets a node named for the first occurrence that uses it. The action key also includes the notes file’s hash, so a copied recording can reuse its render.

files.note: Loads parts, checks instruments and references, and resolves lengths for loops.
Resolves each looping part occurrence and wires each slot to its render while retaining the ordinary loop planner.
Accepts resolved events and hashes a part alongside the instrument and harness.
Creates voice renders for parts and chosen MIDI takes, then places those renders.

checks.text: The loop regression passed: the first occurrence uses a 24,000-sample beat-2 offset at 120 bpm, while later occurrences use 48,000 at 60 bpm. Their stem inputs select the corresponding renders, and equal later occurrences share one render.

files.note: Exercises validation, formatting, cache reuse, tempo edits, and copied takes.
Names a notes placement by the part it references.

groups.title: Recordings land on musical time
intro: When a MIDI performance lands, the output latency comes off each captured event before the track’s tempo map converts its time to ticks. The take’s started_at_ticks stores its distance from the record entry. Moving that entry moves the take by the same musical distance; musical_position records where capture began.

files.note: Converts captured times into ticks and records the take’s distance from its record entry.

checks.text: Open review finding: notes played before a track starts all sound on its first tick. When a take starts before its track does, tickAt clamps both a note's end and start to 0, so this filter keeps every note that ended before the track's first sample, and each lands as a zero-length note at tick 0. A take recorded from bar 1 on a track placed at bar 5 kept three lead-in notes that way. Before this change, the render's negative placement read past them. The fix is to also drop a note whose unclamped end falls before the track's start, and to add that case to land.test.ts.

files.note: Chooses MIDI recording when the track has an instrument.
Finds instruments on tracks without requiring a record entry.
Updates command help for track instruments.
Uses the shared generator-kind helper when naming lanes.

groups.title: The project format describes parts
intro: The documentation explains the notes directory, track instruments, rendering, and copying a take into a part. The sequencer plan records the implemented notes and parts layers and leaves live scheduling to the remaining work.

checks.text: Open review finding: two edited lines break the line wrapping around them. AGENTS.md says to match the wrapping around a Markdown edit. This line runs to 87 columns, and docs/keys.md line 537 runs to 91, among prose wrapped near 72 columns. The fix is to rewrap both paragraphs at the surrounding width.

Open review finding: deleting the record entry, as this step offers, fails field check. With the - record: entry deleted and the take's takes.yaml still in audio/keys/, field check reports no record entry claims audio/keys/ as an error, which stops every build. field choose also refuses a node that has no record entry, so the take is no longer choosable, as the section says it is. The fix is to drop , or delete it, so that the step says to mute the record entry.
